lines.text: Install guh-new Hello, the classic tiny test program, with a normal package manager, and it lands at slash user, slash bin, slash hello.
lines.caption: Install GNU Hello, the classic tiny test program, with a normal package manager, and it lands at slash usr, slash bin, slash hello.

lines.text: Install it with Nix, and it lands somewhere stranger: a directory in slash nix, slash store, whose name starts with thirty-two characters of what looks like noise.
lines.caption: Install it with Nix, and it lands somewhere stranger: a directory in slash nix, slash store, whose name starts with thirty-two characters of what looks like noise.

lines.text: That noise is a hash, and every package Nix installs has one.
lines.caption: That noise is a hash, and every package Nix installs has one.

lines.text: Nix, and Nix O S, the Linux distribution built on it, make some unusual promises.
lines.caption: Nix, and NixOS, the Linux distribution built on it, make some unusual promises.

lines.text: Build the same thing twice and, as far as possible, get the same result.
lines.caption: Build the same thing twice and, as far as possible, get the same result.

lines.text: Keep two versions of a package side by side.
lines.caption: Keep two versions of a package side by side.

lines.text: Roll back an upgrade, for one program or for the whole machine.
lines.caption: Roll back an upgrade, for one program or for the whole machine.

lines.text: Why is there a hash in every path?
lines.caption: Why is there a hash in every path?

lines.text: And how does that one idea deliver all of that?
lines.caption: And how does that one idea deliver all of that?

lines.text: Most package managers put everything in shared places.
lines.caption: Most package managers put everything in shared places.

lines.text: Programs go in slash user, slash bin.
lines.caption: Programs go in slash usr, slash bin.

lines.text: Libraries go in slash user, slash lib.
lines.caption: Libraries go in slash usr, slash lib.

lines.text: Upgrade a library, and the new version overwrites the old one in place.
lines.caption: Upgrade a library, and the new version overwrites the old one in place.

lines.text: Every program that used the old one now gets the new one, whether it was built for it or not.
lines.caption: Every program that used the old one now gets the new one, whether it was built for it or not.

lines.text: Two programs that need different versions of the same library often can't both have what they need.
lines.caption: Two programs that need different versions of the same library often can't both have what they need.

lines.text: Some libraries put a version number in the file name, but most things get exactly one path.
lines.caption: Some libraries put a version number in the file name, but most things get exactly one path.

lines.text: And an upgrade that stops halfway, say the power goes out, leaves some files new and some old: a system that matches no version at all.
lines.caption: And an upgrade that stops halfway, say the power goes out, leaves some files new and some old: a system that matches no version at all.

segments.title: A build is a function of its inputs

lines.text: Nix starts from a different picture.
lines.caption: Nix starts from a different picture.

lines.text: Every package is built from a recipe, which Nix calls a derivation.
lines.caption: Every package is built from a recipe, which Nix calls a derivation.

lines.text: Nix treats that build as a pure function of its inputs, and the inputs are everything the build uses: the source code, the build script, the compiler, the libraries, and every option.
lines.caption: Nix treats that build as a pure function of its inputs, and the inputs are everything the build uses: the source code, the build script, the compiler, the libraries, and every option.

lines.text: On Linux, Nix runs each build isolated by default, so it can use only what it declared.
lines.caption: On Linux, Nix runs each build isolated by default, so it can use only what it declared.

lines.text: Even a downloaded source file has to match a hash written in the recipe.
lines.caption: Even a downloaded source file has to match a hash written in the recipe.

lines.text: Nix computes a hash over all of those inputs, and names the output after it: slash nix, slash store, the hash, then the package name.
lines.caption: Nix computes a hash over all of those inputs, and names the output after it: slash nix, slash store, the hash, then the package name.

lines.text: It can do that before building anything.
lines.caption: It can do that before building anything.

lines.text: On this machine, Nix computed Hello's path from its recipe, and the package then landed exactly there.
lines.caption: On this machine, Nix computed Hello's path from its recipe, and the package then landed exactly there.

lines.text: So the hash is not a checksum of what came out.
lines.caption: So the hash is not a checksum of what came out.

lines.text: It's a name for everything that went in.
lines.caption: It's a name for everything that went in.

segments.title: Change an input, change the path

lines.text: Now change one input.
lines.caption: Now change one input.

lines.text: Here, one option of Hello's build: whether to run its tests.
lines.caption: Here, one option of Hello's build: whether to run its tests.

lines.text: The recipe is different, so the hash is different, and the new Hello gets a new path.
lines.caption: The recipe is different, so the hash is different, and the new Hello gets a new path.

lines.text: A small script called greet runs Hello.
lines.caption: A small script called greet runs Hello.

lines.text: Its inputs include Hello's path, so greet gets a new path too.
lines.caption: Its inputs include Hello's path, so greet gets a new path too.

lines.text: The change ripples to everything built from it.
lines.caption: The change ripples to everything built from it.

lines.text: Cow say doesn't use Hello, so its path stays exactly the same.
lines.caption: Cowsay doesn't use Hello, so its path stays exactly the same.

lines.text: And nothing that was already built gets touched.
lines.caption: And nothing that was already built gets touched.

lines.text: The old Hello and the new Hello now sit side by side in the store, each in its own directory.
lines.caption: The old Hello and the new Hello now sit side by side in the store, each in its own directory.

lines.text: That's how two versions coexist: they can't overwrite each other, because they never share a path.
lines.caption: That's how two versions coexist: they can't overwrite each other, because they never share a path.

lines.text: But Hello isn't self-contained.
lines.caption: But Hello isn't self-contained.

lines.text: It needs other things to run, like the C library.
lines.caption: It needs other things to run, like the C library.

lines.text: So where does it find them, if not in slash user, slash lib?
lines.caption: So where does it find them, if not in slash usr, slash lib?

lines.text: Its files refer to them by their full store paths, hashes included.
lines.caption: Its files refer to them by their full store paths, hashes included.

lines.text: Nix finds those references by scanning the build's output for store paths.
lines.caption: Nix finds those references by scanning the build's output for store paths.

lines.text: Follow them, and the references of those, and you get the package's closure: everything it needs at run time.
lines.caption: Follow them, and the references of those, and you get the package's closure: everything it needs at run time.

lines.text: Hello's closure is five paths: Hello itself, the C library, a library the C library pulls in, another that one needs in turn, and a small runtime library that ships with the compiler and that compiled programs use.
lines.caption: Hello's closure is five paths: Hello itself, the C library, a library the C library pulls in, another that one needs in turn, and a small runtime library that ships with the compiler and that compiled programs use.

lines.text: Copy those five paths to another machine of the same kind, and Hello runs there.
lines.caption: Copy those five paths to another machine of the same kind, and Hello runs there.

lines.text: And things needed only to build it, like the compiler itself, aren't in the list.
lines.caption: And things needed only to build it, like the compiler itself, aren't in the list.

lines.text: So what does it mean to have a program installed?
lines.caption: So what does it mean to have a program installed?

lines.text: In Nix, what you have installed is a generation: a small directory of links into the store.
lines.caption: In Nix, what you have installed is a generation: a small directory of links into the store.

lines.text: Your profile is a link to one generation.
lines.caption: Your profile is a link to one generation.

lines.text: Install Hello: that's generation one.
lines.caption: Install Hello: that's generation one.

lines.text: Install cow say: Nix creates generation two, with links to both, and then switches the profile's link to it, in a single step.
lines.caption: Install cowsay: Nix creates generation two, with links to both, and then switches the profile's link to it, in a single step.

lines.text: There's no moment when the profile is half old and half new.
lines.caption: There's no moment when the profile is half old and half new.

lines.text: It points to one generation, then to the other.
lines.caption: It points to one generation, then to the other.

lines.text: Roll back, and the link switches back to generation one.
lines.caption: Roll back, and the link switches back to generation one.

lines.text: Hello is there, cow say is gone from the profile, and nothing in the store was deleted.
lines.caption: Hello is there, cowsay is gone from the profile, and nothing in the store was deleted.

lines.text: Old generations stay until you delete them.
lines.caption: Old generations stay until you delete them.

lines.text: Only then can Nix's garbage collector remove the store paths nothing else uses.
lines.caption: Only then can Nix's garbage collector remove the store paths nothing else uses.

lines.text: Nix O S applies the same idea to an entire operating system.
lines.caption: NixOS applies the same idea to an entire operating system.

lines.text: You describe the system in configuration dot nix, a file that can pull in others: the packages, the settings, the services to run.
lines.caption: You describe the system in configuration.nix, a file that can pull in others: the packages, the settings, the services to run.

lines.text: Nix builds all of it, the programs, the configuration files, the start-up scripts, into one store path.
lines.caption: Nix builds all of it, the programs, the configuration files, the start-up scripts, into one store path.

lines.text: Here's a minimal configuration, evaluated on this machine.
lines.caption: Here's a minimal configuration, evaluated on this machine.

lines.text: It has one system path.
lines.caption: It has one system path.

lines.text: Add one line, turning on the engine X web server, and the system gets a different path.
lines.caption: Add one line, turning on the nginx web server, and the system gets a different path.

lines.text: Remove the line, and the path is exactly the first one again.
lines.caption: Remove the line, and the path is exactly the first one again.

lines.text: Switching to a new configuration makes a new system generation, and adds it to the boot menu.
lines.caption: Switching to a new configuration makes a new system generation, and adds it to the boot menu.

lines.text: If an upgrade goes wrong, you pick the previous generation when the machine starts, or roll back from the command line.
lines.caption: If an upgrade goes wrong, you pick the previous generation when the machine starts, or roll back from the command line.

lines.text: The link to the new generation switches in one step.
lines.caption: The link to the new generation switches in one step.

lines.text: Bringing the running machine in line with it takes longer: services restart one by one, and a new kernel needs a reboot.
lines.caption: Bringing the running machine in line with it takes longer: services restart one by one, and a new kernel needs a reboot.

lines.text: The hash promises the same inputs.
lines.caption: The hash promises the same inputs.

lines.text: It doesn't always promise the same bytes.
lines.caption: It doesn't always promise the same bytes.

lines.text: Some builds stamp in the date, or vary in small ways from run to run: same path, different bytes.
lines.caption: Some builds stamp in the date, or vary in small ways from run to run: same path, different bytes.

lines.text: A twenty twenty-five study rebuilt about seven hundred thousand packages from old Nix packages snapshots.
lines.caption: A 2025 study rebuilt about seven hundred thousand packages from old Nixpkgs snapshots.

lines.text: Between sixty-nine and ninety-one percent came out bit-for-bit identical, rising over the years.
lines.caption: Between sixty-nine and ninety-one percent came out bit-for-bit identical, rising over the years.

lines.text: And the inputs are only fixed if you fix them.
lines.caption: And the inputs are only fixed if you fix them.

lines.text: Nix packages, the collection the recipes come from, keeps moving.
lines.caption: Nixpkgs, the collection the recipes come from, keeps moving.

lines.text: To get the same inputs next year, pin the exact revision.
lines.caption: To get the same inputs next year, pin the exact revision.

lines.text: Rollback switches the software and its configuration.
lines.caption: Rollback switches the software and its configuration.

lines.text: It doesn't touch your data.
lines.caption: It doesn't touch your data.

lines.text: Say a new version of a database converted its files to a new format.
lines.caption: Say a new version of a database converted its files to a new format.

lines.text: Roll back, and you get the old program, but the files stay converted, and the old program may not be able to read them.
lines.caption: Roll back, and you get the old program, but the files stay converted, and the old program may not be able to read them.

lines.text: So why a hash in every path?
lines.caption: So why a hash in every path?

lines.text: Because the path names a build by everything that went into it.
lines.caption: Because the path names a build by everything that went into it.

lines.text: That's what keeps anything from being overwritten.
lines.caption: That's what keeps anything from being overwritten.

lines.text: Versions coexist because they never share a path.
lines.caption: Versions coexist because they never share a path.

lines.text: Dependencies are exact, because they're referred to by their paths.
lines.caption: Dependencies are exact, because they're referred to by their paths.

lines.text: And an upgrade, or a rollback, is switching one link, for a program or for a whole system.
lines.caption: And an upgrade, or a rollback, is switching one link, for a program or for a whole system.

lines.text: What the hash fixes is the inputs.
lines.caption: What the hash fixes is the inputs.

lines.text: Pin them, and you get the same recipe again; the bytes usually, but not always, follow.
lines.caption: Pin them, and you get the same recipe again; the bytes usually, but not always, follow.

lines.text: And back up your data, because rollback won't.
lines.caption: And back up your data, because rollback won't.
